newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL-OILERS, BLUES AND KINGS WIN IN FIRST NIGHT OF SEASON.
newsitem.headline: NHL-OILERS, BLUES AND KINGS WIN IN FIRST NIGHT OF SEASON.

text.p: Rookie Rem Murray's first NHL goal broke a second-period tie and the Edmonton Oilers defeated the Buffalo Sabres 4-3 in the opening night of the National Hockey League season Friday.

Murray, a free agent who led Edmonton's top minor-league affiliate in scoring last season, backhanded the puck under the crossbar with 6:09 left in the period after goaltender Dominik Hasek made an acrobatic skate save on Todd Marchant's shot.

"The puck got into my skates off the rebound. I was looking down to get it and when I looked up, Hasek was still down, so I just tried to put it upstairs and managed to sneak it under the crossbar," Murray said.
Curtis Joseph stopped only 16 shots for the Oilers.

In St Louis, Grant Fuhr completed a remarkable comeback from knee surgery, making 35 saves and leading the St. Louis Blues to a 4-2 victory over the defending Stanley Cup champion Colorado Avalanche in the season opener for both teams.
Chris Pronger and Jim Campbell each had a goal and an assist for St. Louis, which never trailed.
Fuhr, who played in a league-leading 79 games last season, underwent surgery April 27th after tearing ligaments in his right knee in a first-round playoff game at Toronto.

He protected the Blues' two-goal lead early in the third period when he smothered Adam Deadmarsh's wrist shot from the left goal post and used his glove again to snatch Stephane Yelle's wrister from the top of the slot with just under 14 minutes remaining.
"You don't get nervous, you get excited about it," Fuhr said of his latest comeback.
"That's great," he added, referring to the positive response he got from the crowd. "It makes it all worthwhile. The fans have been great to me here."
in Los Angeles, Stephane Fiset, making his Kings debut, stopped 26 saves for his seventh career shutout as Los Angeles opened the season with 1-0 victory over the New York Islanders.
Ed Olczyk, a free-agent signee this summer for the Kings, scored the games lone goal just hours after the birth of his third son.
Olczyk scored on the power play at 9:18 of the second period by deflecting a shot from Mattias Norstrom past Isles goaltender Eric Fichaud.
